transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (CTO - HelixAI), Noah Rivera (Head of Platform), Arjun Desai (Infra Lead), Laura Finch (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to align scope for upcoming contract extension; main asks are: add EU + APAC regions, test private/VPC pilot for PHI-ish workloads, and a capacity uplift (25%) with burst pool. Customer wants clarity on latency tradeoffs, encryption/KMS story, and timeline for private deployment.

Topics: renewal pricing, region add-on pricing, dedicated vs hosted, private (VPC/on-prem) pilot, SOC2 / audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM options, rollout plan, benchmarks and test plan.

00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. is this still a good time?
00:07 Maya (HelixAI CTO): Yeah, thanks Samir. We have about 50 minutes. trying to get through scope and next steps.
00:14 Samir: Cool. quick agenda: 1) renewal numbers and target capacity 2) regions and residency 3) private pilot scope 4) security + compliance checklist 5) next steps.
00:26 Janelle (Redwood SE): And I'll cover the perf and the benchmark plan mid-call.
00:31 Maya: Perfect. quick context: our usage has grown ~40% qtr over qtr. we're forecasting a 25% uplift for next year. we'd like EU + APAC added and need a path for private serving for sensitive models.
00:45 Noah (HelixAI): Also procurement timeline - target to sign by end of June if pricing and security checks are good.
00:52 Samir: Great, that aligns with what Marcus flagged. Marcus?
00:55 Marcus (Redwood CSM): Yep, just wants to make sure provisioning lead time is explicit so you don't hit cold-start capacity issues when you ramp.
01:05 Janelle: For capacity, do you want reserved dedicated pool or hosted with burst into dedicated? those are the two levers.
01:13 Arjun (HelixAI): We're leaning toward reserved capacity for predictable p95 but also want some burst. curious on the autoscale granularity - if the burst will respect latency targets.
01:24 Janelle: Burst can be configured with pre-warmed nodes and a fast failover routing policy. in our experience if you keep steady-state pinned to a dedicated pool and use a small burst buffer you get best predictability. caveat: cost goes up if burst is oversized.
01:40 Maya: Sounds fine. can you quantify the p95 at target concurrency? our 3ms figure in the deck was internal optimism, not reality.
01:48 Janelle: yeah we ran a sample with gpt-compat small model - at 50 concurrent sessions and sequence 256 we saw p95 ~120-140ms on A100 class nodes — with continuous batching enabled. with quantized variants that drops to ~90-110ms. that's the ballpark.
02:06 Samir: Important to note our public benchmarks are conservative; we'll share the raw spread sheet but you'll want to run with your request mix.
02:15 Maya: Please. also, encryption — we need KMS integration and an HSM option for key custody if possible.
02:22 Janelle: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM via partner integrations is possible for private deployments; there's a separate onboarding step.
02:32 Arjun: For private on-prem, can you confirm the control plane talkback? does telemetry leave our VPC? we need an air-gapped option or at least control plane staying within our network.
02:44 Samir: For Redwood Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option. telemetry and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM; nothing required to leave the VPC unless you opt into hosted telemetry. Air-gapped/on-prem variants are available but take longer to provision.
02:58 Maya: How much longer? we have regulatory windows.
03:02 Samir: Typical private on-prem pilot lead time is 6-8 weeks for the initial sandbox, 10-14 for hardened production, depending on infra availability and contract. can tighten if you pre-commit to capacity.
03:17 Noah: Procurement needs firm numbers for monthly committed GPU hours and regional pricing — will you send a line-item addendum?
03:26 Samir: Yes, I'll send an amendment with committed units, a burst pool definition, and per-region unit pricing.
03:31 Laura (Procurement): On T&Cs, main items: data residency, liability carve-outs for model hallucinations, and indemnity. we'll need a redline.
03:43 Samir: Understood. Legal will provide standard addendum; we can accommodate data residency clauses for the regions we host in. hallucination liability is tricky — we usually offer best-effort language plus carveouts tied to misuse.
03:58 Maya: We'll run the security pack past our infosec — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs currently?
04:04 Janelle: SOC2 Type II yes, ISO underway. we'll attach the security docs. also we have audit logging and per-request trace IDs integrated into the console.
04:16 Arjun: Do you expose token-level costs and per-route latency traces? that's important for our SREs.
04:23 Marcus: Yes, the Console shows token-level spend breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and we can provision tracing hooks.
04:33 Arjun: On network side — support for SAML SSO at org level and RBAC for developer teams?
04:38 Samir: Yep SAML-based SSO and fine-grained RBAC, plus org-level billing and route-level quotas.
04:46 Maya: Back to the private pilot: we want to run a smoke perf test with a 24-hour traffic replay and a 48-hour sustained load test. can Redwood run that in our sandbox?
04:58 Janelle: Yes, we'll provide a test harness. ideally you give us a representative request log and target SLOs. we'll run both hosted and private variants and surface delta metrics.
05:14 Noah: Perfect. how do you handle rolling upgrades and model rollouts? we want canary and automatic fallback in case of regression.
05:23 Janelle: Platform supports canary rollouts by traffic split and automatic fallback to pinned stable model variants. also can tie regressions to eval prompt sets to catch quality drops.
05:36 Maya: Competitor question — we've talked to Anthropic and some larger cloud vendors. do you have a clear differentiation on cost per token and latency for our qps?
05:46 Samir: Short answer: our pricing and runtime focus on predictable unit economics at scale — the differentiator is the unified path between hosted and private with the same API and observability. we'll include a cost model comparing hosted vs dedicated variants for your numbers.
06:05 Arjun: Are there any hard limits for prefix cache or KV sizes in private mode? we rely on fairly long context windows for a subset of models.
06:15 Janelle: KV/prefix caching is configurable. in private deployments we can raise limits; in hosted there's default caps for multi-tenant safety. we'll note specific numbers in the tech spec we send.
06:28 Maya: Okay. timeline wise: if we sign by end of June, provisioning for reserved capacity in EU + APAC — when could we realistically be live?
06:38 Samir: For hosted + dedicated pools in new regions, usually 3-4 weeks after contract if we have capacity available. if you want private on-prem in those regions that's the longer 6-10 week timeline.
06:51 Laura: Procurement — any minimum commitment thresholds?
06:55 Samir: Yes for Dedicated we have monthly minimums. I'll put exact tiers in the quote. there are flexible ramp plans if you want to stage consumption.
07:08 Maya: Let's talk about the pilot acceptance criteria quickly. target p95 under 200ms for critical routes, <1% error rate, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and successful KMS integration.
07:23 Janelle: That sounds achievable. we'll tailor the test plan and confirm exact test payloads.
07:31 Marcus: I'll coordinate the kickoff invite and attach a checklist for infra and security.
07:36 Maya: Great. any blockers from our side? Arjun?
07:39 Arjun: We need the test harness and a small staging cluster that mimics our network egress. also access to an ops contact at Redwood during the load windows.
07:48 Janelle: We'll provide on-call windows and a runbook.
07:52 Laura: one more procurement note: can you include cancellation terms for the reserved capacity in the amendment? we'll want a 60-day notice clause.
08:01 Samir: We'll propose standard termination language with a staged ramp-down. legal can iterate.
08:08 Maya: Okay, let's recap next steps.
08:11 Samir: Recap: Samir sends renewal amendment + region pricing (due 5/21). Janelle shares benchmark sheet and test plan (due 5/24). Marcus books pilot kickoff for week of 5/31. HelixAI to share request logs and SLOs (Arjun, due 5/25). Procurement to share PO timeline (Laura, due 5/23).
08:35 Maya: Good. thanks everyone. appreciate the clarity.
08:39 Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up in writing and attach the security pack.
08:43 Marcus: End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription substituted a few product names (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' for Redwood Dedicated) and misheard acronyms; speaker labels assigned from calendar invite so some overlap when multi-person spoke.
